statement: Steven Roger Fischer (Rongorongo, the Easter Island Script: History, Traditions, Texts, Oxford University Press, 1997) claimed the Santiago Staff tablet encodes a repeating cosmogonic/creation-chant formula ("X copulated with Y; there issued forth Z"), based on a sign he read as "copulate," recurring 564 times. This claim is not accepted by the field: Jacques B.M. Guy (1998 review/critique) and Konstantin Pozdniakov ("Les Bases du Déchiffrement de l'Écriture de l'Ile de Pâques," Journal de la Société des Océanistes, 1996) argue the statistical/structural patterns Fischer relied on arise from the script's own repetitive internal triadic sign-grouping structure and generic Polynesian chant-formula patterns, not from content specific to his proposed reading — making the "decipherment" effectively unfalsifiable.
scholarly_disagreement: Fischer [DECIPHERMENT-CLAIM] vs. Guy and Pozdniakov [SPECIFIC, NAMED REJECTION] — this is a settled minority rejection, not an open dispute; the field does not accept Fischer's reading.
